public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1180

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1180](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1180)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Sh02] Shparlinski, Igor E., *On a question of Erdős and Graham*. Arch. Math. (Basel) (2002),
  445-448.
- [Gl06] Glibichuk, A. A., *Combinatorial properties of sets of residues modulo a prime and the
  Erdős-Graham problem*. Mat. Zametki (2006), 384-395.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos1180

/--
`Represents ε p a s` says that the multiset `s` of denominators `n` with `1 ≤ n ≤ p^ε` and
`n` coprime to `p` has `∑ n⁻¹ = a` in `ZMod p`.
-/
def Represents (ε : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (a : ZMod p) (s : Multiset ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ n ∈ s, 1 ≤ n ∧ (n : ℝ) ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ ε ∧ n.Coprime p) ∧
    (s.map fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ZMod p)⁻¹).sum = a

/--
`C ε` is the least `C` such that, for all primes `p`, every residue modulo `p` is the sum of at
most `C` elements of `{n⁻¹ : 1 ≤ n ≤ p^ε}` (or `0` if no such `C` exists).
-/
noncomputable def C (ε : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {C | ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p, ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, s.card ≤ C ∧ Represents ε p a s}

/--
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist a constant $C_\epsilon$ such that, for all primes $p$, every
residue modulo $p$ is the sum of at most $C_\epsilon$ many elements of
$$\{ n^{-1} : 1\leq n\leq p^\epsilon\}$$
where $n^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $n$ modulo $p$?

The original question was answered in the affirmative, with $C_\epsilon \ll \epsilon^{-3}$, by
Shparlinski [Sh02]. This was improved to $\ll \epsilon^{-2}$ by Glibichuk [Gl06]. It is trivial
that at least $\gg \epsilon^{-1}$ summands are required, and it may be that
$C_\epsilon\leq \epsilon^{-1-o(1)}$ is possible.

See also [540](https://www.erdosproblems.com/540).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1180.lean#L1249"]
theorem erdos_1180 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
    ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, s.card ≤ C ∧ Represents ε p a s := by
  sorry

/-- Shparlinski [Sh02] proved that $C_\epsilon \ll \epsilon^{-3}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1180.variants.shparlinski : ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
    (C ε : ℝ) ≤ K * ε⁻¹ ^ 3 := by
  sorry

/-- Glibichuk [Gl06] proved that $C_\epsilon \ll \epsilon^{-2}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1180.variants.glibichuk : ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
    (C ε : ℝ) ≤ K * ε⁻¹ ^ 2 := by
  sorry

/-- It is trivial that at least $\gg \epsilon^{-1}$ summands are required. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1180.variants.lower_bound : ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
    K * ε⁻¹ ≤ C ε := by
  sorry

/-- Is $C_\epsilon\leq \epsilon^{-1-o(1)}$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1180.variants.optimal : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ →
    ∀ᶠ ε : ℝ in nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0), (C ε : ℝ) ≤ ε⁻¹ ^ (1 + δ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1180

findings.description: The cubic bound uses `C ε`, which is the least bound valid for EVERY prime, including primes that are small relative to ε. This bound cannot be polynomial in ε⁻¹. For any prime p, set ε = log(3/2)/log p. Then p^ε = 3/2, so every admissible denominator is 1. Representing −1 modulo p therefore requires at least p−1 summands, giving C ε ≥ p−1, whereas K * ε⁻¹ ^ 3 grows only like K(log p)^3. The exact negation of this declaration was proved in the scratch experiment without sorry-backed dependencies.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1180 attributes C_ε ≪ ε⁻³ to Shparlinski. Its quantitative summary suppresses a necessary large-prime qualification: the cited improvement [Gl06], https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11006-006-0040-8, explicitly begins with ε>0 and 'a sufficiently large prime p>2'. Croot's arXiv:math/0403360, Section II opening paragraph, separately explains that extending qualitative existence to small primes requires enlarging N(ε,k). Such an enlargement does not preserve the stated polynomial dependence on ε.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a separate asymptotic summand bound, for example `sInf {B : ℕ | ∃ P : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, P ≤ p → p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p, ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, s.card ≤ B ∧ Represents ε p a s}`, in the quantitative variants. Alternatively put an ε-dependent prime threshold directly into this theorem. The qualitative all-primes theorem need not change.

findings.description: This asserts the quadratic estimate for the all-primes minimum `C ε`, rather than for representations at sufficiently large primes depending on ε. It is false: taking ε = log(3/2)/log p forces C ε ≥ p−1 because the only allowed denominator is 1, while the proposed upper bound is O((log p)^2). I proved the negation of the exact Lean statement, using the independently verified qualitative existence theorem to ensure that `C` is a genuine minimum rather than its empty-set fallback.
findings.source_evidence: Glibichuk [Gl06], published abstract at https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11006-006-0040-8: 'Consider an arbitrary ε > 0 and a sufficiently large prime p > 2.' It then gives N = 8(⌊1/ε + 1/2⌋ + 1)^2 summands. The source explicitly allows the prime threshold to depend on ε; the definition of `C` does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `C` here by the least bound valid for all sufficiently large primes, with a threshold quantified after ε, or state the quadratic representation bound directly with `∃ P, ∀ p ≥ P, p.Prime → ...`. Retain an absolute implied constant K.

findings.description: With the file's all-primes `C`, the right-hand side is already false: even δ=1 fails arbitrarily close to ε=0, by the same family ε=log(3/2)/log p. This was proved in Lean without sorry dependencies. Thus it cannot serve as an open refinement of the large-prime quantitative bounds. There is a source ambiguity, however: the website itself uses 'all primes' in the qualitative question and then reuses C_ε in the optimality remark without explicitly introducing a prime threshold. The literal website reading agrees with Lean, so this is a request to clarify the intended quantitative constant, not an unqualified claim that the formalization differs from that literal wording.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1180 says, after the Shparlinski and Glibichuk bounds, that 'it may be that C_ε ≤ ε^{-1-o(1)} is possible.' Its initial question quantifies over all primes. The primary Glibichuk statement instead explicitly assumes sufficiently large p: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11006-006-0040-8.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify whether the optimality question concerns the least summand bound after an ε-dependent prime threshold. If so, use that asymptotic constant in the existing ε→0⁺ formulation. Do not merely fill the answer slot with False if the intended question is the unresolved refinement of the large-prime result.

reformulations.difference: The qualitative theorem quantifies over every prime, whereas the primary quantitative result is formulated for sufficiently large primes.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Without prescribing growth of the constant in ε, an eventual-prime bound B with threshold P extends to all primes using max(B,P): for p<P, represent a by a.val copies of denominator 1. Conversely, an all-primes bound immediately supplies an eventual-prime bound. This explains why the qualitative theorem is sound even though transferring the polynomial estimates to the all-primes minimum is not.

sources_consulted: T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problem #1180, https://www.erdosproblems.com/1180 — full text and formulas recovered through https://r.jina.ai/http://erdosproblems.com/1180 using its HTML output.
Erdős and Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), p. 103; scanned original at https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf.
Shparlinski, On a question of Erdős and Graham (2002), published abstract: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00013-002-8269-2.
Glibichuk, Combinational properties of sets of residues modulo a prime and the Erdős–Graham problem (2006), published abstract: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11006-006-0040-8.

Croot, Sums of the Form 1/x_1^k + ... + 1/x_n^k Modulo a Prime, arXiv:math/0403360v2: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0403360 and LaTeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0403360, particularly Sections I and II.
could_not_verify: Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.optimal: the intended prime quantifier in the source's optimality remark remains ambiguous. Its literal all-primes reading matches Lean and is provably false, whereas the surrounding primary quantitative result uses sufficiently large primes. This ambiguity is recorded as questionable above.
review.notes: Checked all seven declarations, the relevant Mathlib definitions, quantifiers, casts, answer slots, and boundary cases. In particular, `Represents` correctly counts repetitions and excludes noninvertible denominators; empty sums represent zero; `C 0 = 0` is documented and outside the positive-ε domains. No defect was found in the qualitative theorem or the lower-bound variant. The pinned external proof compiled successfully, and its list-based conclusion was transported to the repository's multiset statement. `/workspace/review/full_counterexample.lean` proves `Review1180.shparlinski_variant_false`, `Review1180.glibichuk_variant_false`, and `Review1180.optimal_rhs_false`; all have only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as axioms. The current source records the main problem as proved and still presents the optimal bound as a possibility; no stale-status finding is asserted.

not_demonstrated.reason: The exact negation requires an unbounded family of primes and the comparison p−1 ≫ (log p)^3; a fixed numerical example cannot defeat the unrestricted existential K. It also requires the nontrivial qualitative existence result to ensure C ε is not the empty-set fallback. The previously compiled, sorry-free disproof is substantially longer than the requested trivial demonstration.

The exact negation likewise requires an unbounded prime family, logarithmic growth estimates, and nonemptiness of the set defining C ε. A finite computation would not refute the existential constant K. The existing rigorous disproof does not satisfy the short-proof requirement.

submission.summary: Neither reported bound admits a short demonstration that I can honestly supply under these rules. The longer verified disproofs remain in /workspace/review/full_counterexample.lean, but I have not hidden them behind imports or used sorry-backed declarations. No trivial_proof.lean was created.
submission.gave_up_reason: The available exact disproofs require substantial auxiliary mathematics and a nontrivial existence theorem; they are not trivial proofs in the requested sense.

not_fixed.reason: Left unchanged as instructed for questionable findings; the source's intended prime quantifier remains ambiguous.

submission.summary: Replaced both bounds on the all-primes minimum C with explicit representation bounds for primes above an ε-dependent threshold, retaining an absolute constant K. Updated the corresponding quantitative descriptions. The edited file compiles with only the expected declaration-uses-sorry warnings.
